Christmas came early for the global far right, as images showed tens of
thousands of migrants from Morocco breaching the borders of the Spanish
enclave Ceuta. From [Donald Trump ](https://zeteo.com/p/the-ugly-misogyny-of-
trumps-movement?r=3uiw9m)to [Nigel Farage](https://zeteo.com/p/breaking-nigel-
farage-resigns-from?r=3uiw9m), the far right reacted exactly how you would
think - by stirring up fear about a fake "invasion" and weaponizing the so-
called crisis to rally their bases. Trump
[said](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/31/politics/video/spain-ceuta-morocco-
trump-immigration-midterms-digvid) the surge should be used as a "talking
point" in the midterm election, while Farage
[used](https://x.com/Nigel_Farage/status/2082880424452207084?s=20) it to
promote his Reform UK party.

There's a lot of misinformation, racism, and xenophobia driving the hysterical
response from the right in the U.S., UK, and European Union. So, what really
happened? Here are nine things you should know about the fake "invasion" of
Spain:

### **1\. Ceuta Is Not in Europe**

Although the six-mile-long peninsula is a Spanish enclave, Ceuta isn't in
mainland Spain. The city lies on Morocco's northern coast. It has been under
[Spanish control](https://apnews.com/article/spain-morocco-immigration-
european-union-8f023984a310276c619929102b4f909a) since 1580 and is one of two
Spanish cities that form the European Union's only _land_ borders with Africa,
the other being Melilla. While Ceuta is
[part](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/07/31/world/spain-ceuta-migrants-
morocco) of the EU and the Schengen Area, it operates under special rules that
restrict people from entering mainland Spain and the rest of the EU.

### **2\. At Least 80% of the Migrants Have Already Returned to Morocco
Voluntarily**

More than 48,000 [people](https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ceuta-border-
crisis-live-more-than-49000-migrants-cross-into-spanish-enclave-2026-07-31/)
of the estimated 60,000 who breached Ceuta's border have now
[returned](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SDhN6KeuzyI) to Morocco
voluntarily, a clear contradiction of the claims of many right-wingers who
called it an 'invasion.' At least 57 people died during the journey.
